title: Unit 2: In-Context Learning — Zero-Shot, Few-Shot & Chain-of-Thought

topics.title: Few-Shot Exemplar Selection and Formatting
topics.starter_question: If zero-shot prompting fails on an edge-case task, how should you structure few-shot examples to guide the model effectively?

expectations.text: Provide diverse and balanced input-output demonstration pairs covering edge cases and expected failure modes.
Keep demonstration syntax, label conventions, and delimiters strictly uniform across all exemplars.

misconceptions.label: Skewing few-shot exemplar distributions toward one class
misconceptions.description: Including disproportionately more positive or negative examples, biasing the model to predict the dominant label.

misconceptions.label: Assuming earlier exemplars carry the same weight as the final exemplar
misconceptions.description: Ignoring the tendency of LLMs to disproportionately attend to the nearest preceding demonstration before completion.

topics.title: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Prompting
topics.starter_question: Why does adding 'Think step by step' improve accuracy on multi-step reasoning problems, and where should the reasoning appear relative to the final answer?

expectations.text: Chain-of-Thought prompting forces the generation of intermediate reasoning tokens before predicting the final answer.
Placing the rationale trace before the final answer allows subsequent output tokens to be conditioned on explicit logic.

misconceptions.label: Expecting Chain-of-Thought to resolve factual knowledge retrieval gaps
misconceptions.description: Believing step-by-step reasoning compensates for missing facts rather than decomposing complex logic and calculations.

misconceptions.label: Placing the final answer before the intermediate reasoning steps
misconceptions.description: Assuming the model can reason backwards after already committing to the final answer token distribution.
